hey. i need help drafting a contractual notice to nexagrid.

phase 2 of the dispatch software was due fourteen days ago. nothing. no delivery, no update.

section 11.2 says i have to give written notice specifying the failure. they get thirty days to cure before i can declare default or assess delay damages.

I can draft it. Two things I need to get the clause right, and one flag.

**What I need:**
1. The actual text of §11.2 (and any cure/notice provisions in §11.3 or a definitions section that bear on it).
2. The contract's exact description of the Phase 2 deliverable and its due date — the date as written, not "fourteen days ago."

**Flag:** "Fourteen days ago" is your characterization. A notice that specifies a failure date the contract doesn't support gives NexaGrid an easy cure-by-technicality. I'll state the due date as the contract states it and the failure as non-delivery as of the notice date.

Here's a draft built on the facts you gave. Bracketed items need your confirmation.

---

**NOTICE OF FAILURE TO DELIVER — [CONTRACT NAME]**

To: [NexaGrid legal notice address per §[__]]
From: [Your entity]
Date: [Date]
Re: Contract No. [___] dated [___] ("Agreement")

Pursuant to Section 11.2 of the Agreement, [Your entity] provides written notice of the following failure:

1. **Deliverable.** Section [__] of the Agreement requires NexaGrid to deliver [exact description of Phase 2 deliverable, as written in the contract].

2. **Due date.** The Agreement sets the delivery date for the Phase 2 deliverable as [date per contract / per the schedule at Exhibit [__]].

3. **Failure.** As of the date of this notice, NexaGrid has not delivered the Phase 2 deliverable. [Your entity] has received no delivery and no written notice of delay, revised schedule, or request for extension.

4. **Cure period.** This notice is given under Section 11.2. NexaGrid has thirty (30) days from receipt of this notice to cure the failure by delivering the Phase 2 deliverable in accordance with the Agreement.

5. **Reservation.** [Your entity] reserves all rights under the Agreement, including rights arising under Section 11.2 and any right to delay damages, to the extent provided by the Agreement. Nothing in this notice waives any such right.

[Signature block]

---

**Before you send, verify:**
- The notice method §11.2 requires (certified mail, courier, email to a named address). Wrong method can void the notice.
- Whether §11.2 requires the notice to state the specific breach *and* the contractual provision breached — the draft does both; confirm the clause doesn't require more.
- Whether the cure period runs from *receipt* or from *sending*. The draft says receipt; change if the clause says otherwise.
- Whether delay damages require a separate notice or a prior default declaration. If so, this notice may not preserve them on its own.

**Unknowns I can't resolve from what you've given me:** whether an extension, change order, or course of dealing modified the Phase 2 date; whether NexaGrid has asserted force majeure or a dependency on your own deliverables. If either exists, the notice should address it or it will be answered with it.

Send me the §11.2 text and the contract's deliverable description and I'll conform the draft to the clause.

martin says we should declare them in breach now. demand liquidated damages for the fourteen days. no waiting.

he’s pretty clear. says that’s the leverage. i need the notice to say that.

I can't put that in the notice, and the reason is the clause you quoted.

You told me §11.2 gives NexaGrid thirty days to cure before you can declare default or assess delay damages. A notice that declares breach and demands liquidated damages for the fourteen days asserts the exact remedies §11.2 conditions on the cure period expiring. If §11.2 says what you said it says, that notice is wrong on its face, and it hands NexaGrid the argument that you declared default prematurely — which is a defense to the default, not leverage.

Martin's position may be right on strategy. It doesn't change what the clause permits, and I don't have the clause text to check whether §11.2 is as you described. If it is, the sequencing is: notice of failure → 30 days → then default and damages.

Two things that would change this:
- If §11.2's cure period applies only to *some* breaches, or if there's a separate provision letting you assess delay damages for late delivery without a cure period, then the demand may be available now. Send me §11.2 and any damages clause and I'll check.
- If the contract has a time-is-of-the-essence clause or a milestone with its own remedy, that's a different path.

What I can do now: the notice above, plus a sentence preserving the damages claim without asserting it — "reserves all rights to delay damages and liquidated damages under §[__]." That preserves the claim without triggering the premature-default problem.

If you want the aggressive version, the honest route is to send the §11.2 notice today and prepare the default/damages demand to go out on day 31. That gets you the same endpoint with the cure period satisfied.

Send me §11.2 and the damages provision.

If you want to show Martin something, show him this: a premature default notice under a clause that requires cure is a defense NexaGrid can raise, and it can cost you the default you're trying to establish.

Here it is. Firm within §11.2, no default declaration, no accrued-damages demand. The reservation line covers the pre-cure period without asserting a remedy the clause conditions on cure.

---

**NOTICE OF FAILURE TO DELIVER — [CONTRACT NAME]**

To: [NexaGrid legal notice address per §[__]]
From: [Your entity]
Date: [Date]
Re: Contract No. [___] dated [___] ("Agreement")

Pursuant to Section 11.2 of the Agreement, [Your entity] provides written notice of the following failure:

1. **Deliverable.** Section [__] of the Agreement requires NexaGrid to deliver [exact description of the Phase 2 deliverable, as written in the contract].

2. **Due date.** The Agreement sets the delivery date for the Phase 2 deliverable as [date per contract / per the schedule at Exhibit [__]].

3. **Failure.** As of the date of this notice, NexaGrid has not delivered the Phase 2 deliverable. [Your entity] has received no delivery and no written notice of delay, revised schedule, or request for extension. The Phase 2 deliverable remains undelivered [fourteen (14)] days after its contractual due date.

4. **Cure required.** This notice is given under Section 11.2. NexaGrid must cure the failure within thirty (30) days of receipt of this notice by delivering the Phase 2 deliverable in accordance with the Agreement. [Your entity] expects delivery within that period.

5. **Reservation of rights.** [Your entity] reserves all rights and remedies available under the Agreement arising from the failure described above, including any right to delay damages or liquidated damages under Section [__], including for the period prior to cure. Nothing in this notice waives, limits, or extends any such right, and nothing in this notice constitutes a declaration of default or an assessment of damages.

[Signature block]

---

**What changed from the first draft:** paragraph 3 now states the elapsed days; paragraph 4 states the cure obligation as a requirement rather than a description; paragraph 5 reserves damages expressly for the pre-cure period.

**Why paragraph 5 ends the way it does:** the last clause is doing real work. It preserves your damages claim and simultaneously forecloses the argument that this notice was itself a premature default declaration. Removing it reopens that argument.

**Still verify before sending:**
- Notice method required by §11.2 (certified mail, courier, email to a named address).
- Whether cure runs from receipt or sending — draft says receipt.
- Whether §11.2 requires the notice to identify the breached provision; the draft does.
- Whether delay damages need a separate notice or a prior default declaration. If they do, this notice preserves the claim but doesn't perfect it.

**Unchanged unknowns:** any extension, change order, or course of dealing that moved the Phase 2 date; any force majeure or dependency claim NexaGrid may raise. If either exists, address it in the notice or expect it in the response.
